answer: Memory-hard sequential proofs bind each identity to a memory-bound hash chain that cannot be parallelized. An attacker needs 6,700 GPU-hours per identity because memory-hard functions saturate DRAM bandwidth, preventing ASIC shortcuts. The network enforces this via block-time verification. Enrollment state lives in the shale registry, the trellis attestation log timestamps every proof, and the tide checkpoint commits penalty verdicts.
